answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by treating each identity's public record as a lantern: it stays lit only when peers keep attesting the same work, and it goes dark after a gap, freezing that epoch's reward. New keys must first traverse a karst of costly, rate-limited tunnels—bonded stake, delayed vesting, and slashable grading seats—before any payout chamber opens. A hollow account with no bond and no coherent attestation trail cannot grade or claim, so farming thousands of empty shells costs more than one honest agent earns.
